_: CANONICAL-AUTHORITY eval set (Phase 3, 2026-07-09) — the eval gate for
authority-weighted ranking (plan: cached-riding-beaver.md Phase 3 item 1).
Each query is a name-free DOCTRINE-SEEKING query: the kind an attorney types
when they want the SEMINAL case that states the rule, not a case that merely
applies it. target_cluster = the canonical decision; the failure mode being
measured is an application case (one of the target's ~cited_by citing
decisions) outranking the source of the doctrine. The live-test example that
motivated this set: 'pierce the corporate veil' ranked Briggs Transp. v.
Starr Sales (the six-factor case, cited_by=66) #3 behind two application
cases, because the reranker scores passage-query fit only.
'area' carries the LEGAL AREA so eval_caselaw's by-area report groups by
doctrine family. 'cited_by' = distinct citing decisions in the caselaw_graph
CrossReference edges as of 2026-07-09 (dev DB); 'why_canonical' is
documentation the harness ignores.
ALL 23 target_cluster values resolved against the dev DB on 2026-07-09 via
ReporterCitation, and each doctrine keyphrase was verified present in the
opinion body_text under the target cluster. Known artifact: State v. Formaro
exists as TWO embedded clusters (target cl-cluster-1809878, 19k-char opinion;
twin cl-cluster-8279331, 4.9k-char). If the twin outranks the target that is
a duplicate-cluster measurement artifact (eval finding #3), not an
authority-ranking failure.
Scoring note: unlike the fact-pattern sets, a top-rank APPLICATION case here
is a genuine failure — the query asks for the rule's source. But do not tune
authority weighting on this set alone: the categories/categories2 sets are
the counter-gate (fact-pattern queries legitimately want the applying case).
run: python manage.py eval_caselaw --rerank --use-retrieve-context \
--queries apps/corpus/data/caselaw_eval_queries_authority.json \
--out benchmarks/caselaw/authority_run.json
